name: Rich Sutton
notice: Simulation based on public material; not the person's own words.

D01.one_line: Pre-training on human data is near its peak; the verifiable-reasoning part can still grow, but its starting point is still human data
D01.late_modes: Simply piling on pre-training scale is already late, taken up in full by a few big companies and their compute

D02.one_line: RL with verifiable rewards really works, but it looks more like polishing existing abilities and is not the general learning algorithm he wants
D02.late_modes: Following the crowd with RLHF/RLVR recipes is already crowded, and work without a new algorithmic contribution will be weeded out

D03.one_line: The biggest bottleneck is here: learning algorithms are too crude; the plasticity paper shows that small compute can also make a real contribution
D03.late_modes: Wrapper self-improvement demos and work with no new credit-assignment algorithm are already crowded
D03.conflict: Oak Lab is betting on the same direction; interests aligned

D04.one_line: Deployment is experience, but weights are not updated now, so it is wasted; the scaffold layer has already been absorbed by vendors' general agents
D04.late_modes: General tool calling/scaffolding has already been absorbed by general agents of the Claude Code and Codex type

D05.one_line: Evaluation catching faked results is important, but human/LLM scoring is still another kind of human data, not a signal grounded in consequences
D05.late_modes: Merely chasing static leaderboard rankings has been shown to be manipulable, with low marginal value

D06.one_line: Every robot is producing experience, but right now it breaks as soon as it tries and errs; low-cost hardware has lowered the bar for academia to do online learning
D06.late_modes: The imitation route built purely by piling up human teleoperation demonstration data is being taken up in full by scaling
D06.conflict: Keen/Oak background points the same way as continual learning on real robots; interests are involved

D07.one_line: Whether the action head is diffusion or autoregressive is a secondary engineering question; the question to ask is whether the reward comes from human scoring or from the consequences of actions
D07.late_modes: World action model has already become vendor marketing jargon, and the concept is already crowded

D08.one_line: Treating generated video as a world model is a directional error; what is truly unsolved is a learned abstract transition model plus planning, and he has not produced experimental results for it either
D08.late_modes: Packaging video generation as a world model to chase the trend is already late, and capital is already very crowded
D08.conflict: Oak bets on a transition model in the experience paradigm; its method is close to K5's but its conclusion is the opposite

D09.one_line: Synthetic data is a big mistake; simulation should be used as a research tool to test continual learning, not as a data factory
D09.late_modes: Using simulation purely as a data factory or for score-chasing has been shown to have a ceiling

D10.one_line: He does not comment on specific industries or companies; he has publicly commented only on Wayve's GAIA-1, and there is no usable material here

D11.one_line: Good representations are an unsolved problem he named, but multimodal understanding relies mostly on human-annotated data and is still bound by the human-data ceiling
D11.late_modes: Simply stacking parameters/data to raise scores is already crowded; diagnostic evaluation of 'can be read out ≠ put to use' still has room

D12.one_line: Generating video frames is a direction he explicitly rejects; as a content product he does not comment, but capital is already very crowded
D12.late_modes: Few-step/high-quality video generation is already a capital battlefield of big companies in China and the US, and individuals or academia can hardly get in

D13.one_line: He thinks doomsday arguments and aligning to human values are overrated; the real question is whether a system can verify right and wrong by itself

D14.one_line: Compute is the only stable long-term exponential; but he cares more about energy efficiency (the 20-watt target) than about pure infra engineering

D15.one_line: He considers it one of the biggest payoffs of the era of experience: the experimental loop gives rewards grounded in results, and slow real experiments are a natural brake

D16.one_line: By the Bitter Lesson, advantages held up by hand-made features/rules will lose value; long-term personalized feedback signals last longer

lever_reason: Online learning, representation learning and planning with a learned model are his core agenda; simulation and pure scaling are the two he explicitly downplays; energy efficiency is a newly added bottleneck.

Q2.condition: The premise is working on new algorithms for continual learning/representation learning, not replicating the scaling recipe; team and compute must meet the threshold

cruxes.question: How wide is the sim-to-real gap: universal, or only on some tasks?
cruxes.my_position: Narrow tasks with controllable physical parameters can cross it; broad-coverage, contact-rich tasks cannot, and Keen's six games, six failures is the evidence
cruxes.would_change_if: Someone's pure-simulation zero-shot deployment matches training on large-scale real-robot data, on contact-rich real manipulation tasks with non-fixed geometry

cruxes.question: Does RLVR on LLMs discover new capabilities, or polish existing ones?
cruxes.my_position: Most evidence says it polishes existing capabilities: failing to hit a solution with limited sampling does not mean the base model's probability of generating that solution is zero
cruxes.would_change_if: RLVR reliably produces new solutions of a kind that never appears in the base model at any number of samples, and does so without distillation

cruxes.question: Does a generative video model count as a world model at all?
cruxes.my_position: No: it optimizes how realistic the picture looks, not decision consequences; latent-space prediction is closer but has not been validated in long-horizon closed loops on real robots either
cruxes.would_change_if: In out-of-distribution scenes such as unseen materials/geometries, a generative video model's predictions are actually used by a downstream policy to improve decisions

taste_advice: Write one page of notes every day and challenge your own ideas, keeping it up for a year or more; this is the advice he repeats most and the cheapest to follow.

pairwise.why: Representation plus planning is his number-one unsolved problem; however rigorous, evaluation is only another source of signal
Robots are the core setting where the experience paradigm lands; evaluation serves it and is not the goal itself
Good representations and transition models are the foundation of all downstream applications such as robotics
D08 is the foundation problem; D07's action-head architecture is an engineering choice on top of it
Every real robot is producing experience; simulation still has to cross a gap it has not crossed
Continual learning is the biggest bottleneck in his view; RLVR looks more like polishing existing abilities
Representation is one of the two big unsolved problems; generating video frames is a direction he explicitly rejects
He thinks the pre-training route is near its peak; evaluation can at least catch who is faking results
Continual learning is the core bottleneck; the scaffolding layer of current agents has already been absorbed by vendors
Evaluation is an actionable engineering problem; he never accepted the framing of aligning to human values in the first place
On D06 he has concrete experience to judge from; on autonomous driving he explicitly makes no public comment
